beats.html:
Before candy,
there were soul cakes.

Small spiced cakes,
marked with a cross.

The poor went door to door
and were given the cakes.
Asking at the door
began as feeding the poor.

beats.html:
The Owens house
in Practical Magic
was mostly hollow.

It was built on bare land
in Washington state.

It came down the day after
filming wrapped.
The house we all wanted
only stood for a season.

beats.html:
Day of the Dead grew
from 2 sets of roots.

Aztec, Toltec, Olmec and Maya
traditions saw death
as life continuing.

Those rituals blended with
All Saints and All Souls.
Death as a continuation,
not an ending.

beats.html:
A French abbot gave the dead
their own day.

Odilo of Cluny set
November 2 for prayer
for all the dead.

By the late 1200s it was kept
almost everywhere
in the Western church.
Remembering the dead
became a shared act.
